headline: Trump notifies Congress: Military conflict with Iran has resumed
summary: President Donald Trump has formally notified Congress that military operations against Iran began again on July 7, citing violations of a previous memorandum of understanding.
details: US President Donald Trump has officially informed Congress that military conflict with Iran has resumed. This announcement triggers a new 60-day window during which the President can conduct military operations against Iran without congressional approval.

In a formal letter, Trump stated that military operations resumed on July 7. He described these actions as part of his constitutional duty to protect US citizens, national security, and foreign policy interests.

The decision follows allegations that Tehran violated a memorandum of understanding signed on June 17. Specifically, the US claims Iran attacked commercial ships traveling through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Trump administration had previously attempted diplomatic solutions, including a two-week ceasefire announced on April 7, which was later extended. However, tensions have escalated sharply in recent days.
Trump also announced the reinstatement of a blockade on Iranian ships in the Gulf and measures to ensure continued maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

Under the War Powers Act, the US President must notify Congress within 48 hours of starting military operations. Such operations must typically conclude within 60 days unless Congress grants an extension.

Opposition Democrats and some anti-war Republicans argue that the administration is misinterpreting the War Powers Act. They claim the previous 60-day window should have expired on May 1, regardless of the ceasefire.

Last month, both the Senate and House of Representatives passed a resolution calling for the withdrawal of US forces from ongoing military operations in Iran, reflecting deep congressional concern over the prolonged conflict.

headline: World Cup: France and Spain clash in semi-final
summary: A high-stakes battle between Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as France seeks a third consecutive final and Spain aims for glory.
details: France and Spain face off in the first semi-final of the World Cup on Wednesday. This marks only the second time these two giants have met in the tournament, with France winning their 2006 encounter 3-1.

France aims to emulate Germany and Brazil by reaching three consecutive World Cup finals. Meanwhile, Spain enters the match with an impressive record, having lost only one of their last 27 major tournament matches since 2018.

Kylian Mbappe is a central figure for France, tied with Lionel Messi for the Golden Boot race with eight goals. He holds the record for the most World Cup knockout goals (12), but has yet to score in a semi-final.
Spain's Lamine Yamal has become a nightmare for France, scoring three goals against them in two matches across the Euro 2024 semi-finals and the 2025 UEFA Nations League.

Managerial milestones are also on the line. France's Didier Deschamps will overtake Helmut Schön for the record of most World Cup matches managed, while Spain's Luis de la Fuente remains unbeaten in 13 matches across major tournaments.
Spain's road to the semi-finals included victories over Austria, Portugal, and Belgium, while France dominated their path with wins against Sweden, Paraguay, and Morocco.
